s1.syndrome_frame: Acute episodic syndrome with abdominal pain, vomiting, and transient neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Diaphoresis, mucocutaneous paleness, dizziness, dysarthria, incoherent speech, and lack of eye contact
Frontal headache and persistent nausea after the episode
key_facts: 8-year-old boy with no significant past medical history
30-minute history of generalized abdominal pain followed by a single episode of vomiting
Developed diaphoresis, mucocutaneous paleness, dizziness, dysarthria, incoherent speech, and lack of eye contact during the episode
Episode lasted 10 minutes without loss of consciousness, abnormal movements, or sphincter relaxation
Reported a frontal headache and persistent nausea after the episode
Had a similar episode 18 months earlier
No personal or family history of epilepsy or neurological disorders
Normal vital signs except for blood pressure above the 95th percentile for age
Neurologic examination revealed confusion and disorientation
Normal complete blood count, serum chemistries, and electrolytes
Normal brain MRI with an epilepsy protocol

shortlist.why_kept: Transient neurological symptoms and abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Migraine with abdominal aura
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent headaches with vomiting and prior similar diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including generalized abdominal pain, vomiting, diaphoresis, and headache, are consistent with migraine with abdominal aura. The episode's short duration and lack of loss of consciousness or abnormal movements also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cyclic vomiting syndrome
rejected.why: Absence of metabolic disturbances and normal laboratory studies

rejected.label: Familial hemiplegic migraine
rejected.why: No family history of migraine or neurological disorders, and no hemiplegic symptoms

rejected.label: Basilar migraine
rejected.why: No symptoms suggestive of brainstem involvement, such as ataxia or visual field defects
